away.name: Scott Wedgewood
away.news: Surprisingly, Colorado hasn't turned to Scott Wedgewood this season and has rolled with Blackwood between the pipes for the first three games. Wedgewood's tremendous 2025-26 season, posting a 2.02 GAA and .921 SV% in 45 appearances (31-6-6), should at least earn him close to a timeshare by season's end, even if the team is showing early-season favour for Blackwood. Colorado enters Thursday's contest as significant -235 road favourites against a struggling Calgary team that has been outscored 16-3 through three games (0-3-0).

home.name: Devin Cooley
home.news: Cooley had a terrific first season as a full-time NHLer, serving primarily as Dustin Wolf's backup, posting a solid 2.69 GAA and .909 SV% in 31 appearances (10-10-6) for a poor Calgary Flames team. The 29-year-old Cooley struggled in his only 2026-27 outing, allowing three goals on 25 shots (.880 SV%) in a 4-1 loss to the Vancouver Canucks, but hopes to improve Thursday against the Colorado Avalanche. The Flames enter Thursday's contest as sizeable +207 home underdogs against an Avalanche team coming off a disappointing final-minute 3-2 loss to the Winnipeg Jets yesterday.

away.name: Sergei Bobrovsky
away.news: Bobrovsky's early-season introduction to the Maple Leafs hasn't been overly encouraging. Still, he will likely return to the crease on Thursday against the Vegas Golden Knights in search of his first victory. The 38-year-old Bobrovsky has allowed six goals on 53 shots (.887 SV%) through two games this season (0-2-0). The Maple Leafs enter Thursday as +151 road underdogs against a Golden Knights team coming off a 6-2 win over the Seattle Kraken.

home.name: Adin Hill
home.news: The Golden Knights have turned to Carter Hart in three of four games this season, but Hill played well in his only outing and will return to the crease on Thursday against the Toronto Maple Leafs. The 30-year-old Hill saved 18 of 20 shots in an October 4th 3-2 victory over the Vancouver Canucks. Hill is hoping to bounce back after an ugly 2025-26 season, posting a 3.04 GAA and .871 SV% in 27 appearances (10-9-6). The Golden Knights enter Thursday as -164 home favourites against a 2-2-0 Maple Leafs team.
